questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.

questions.solution:

  •  "Diversity" means a range of different things or people.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".

Additional Information

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 4.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "monitoring."
 Key Points
  • "Monitoring" means keeping track of something and making sure it's running smoothly.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Additional Information

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank(1)

The correct answer is 'traced'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in blank no 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate word to fill in blank no 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'a'.

Key Points

  • The given passage is talking about the effect of the coronavirus pandemic in the US.
  • Let's refer to this line from the passage, ''The coronavirus pandemic has brought most of the US to ___(1)___ standstill''.
  • In the given sentence, the noun 'standstill' is a non-specific or non-particular noun.
  • 'A' is a determiner used to modify non-specific or non-particular nouns.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank before the non-specific noun 'standstill' is the determiner 'a'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore the other options:
    • That is a determiner used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.
    • Their is a determiner which means belonging to or associated with the people or things previously mentioned or easily identified.
    • The is a determiner used to refer to specific or particular nouns.

  • दिए गए वाक्य में, noun ' standstill ' एक गैर-विशिष्ट या गैर-विशेष संज्ञा है ।
  • ' A ' एक Determiner है जो गैर-विशिष्ट या गैर-विशेष संज्ञा को संशोधित करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in blank no 5.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'previous.'

Key Points

  • Let us discuss the meanings of the given options:

  • The given sentence is trying to convey that the older generation only switched to a new product when the former one's useful life ended.
     

Correct Paragraph: While the older generation of Indians would buy a new product only when the (1) previous one's useful life had ended, the young generation ______(2)______ to fall for novelty. Young people want the ______(3)______ gadgets because they have money and more ______(4)______ to such goods. They are made to believe, by ______(5)______ publicity, that the new products will enhance their happiness.

Additional Information      

  • Let us see the synonyms of the given words:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'latest.'

Key Points

  • Late is the positive degree and Later is the comparative degree of the word 'late.'
  • 'Latest' is the superlative degree of 'late.'
  • Latter is also a comparative degree.
  • We use a superlative to say that a thing or person is the most of a group.
  • When we use a superlative adjective ('the tallest student') before the noun, we generally use it with 'the'.
     

Correct Paragraph: While the older generation of Indians would buy a new product only when the (1) previous one's useful life had ended, the young generation (2) tends to fall for novelty. Young people want the (3) latest gadgets because they have money and more ______(4)______ to such goods. They are made to believe, by ______(5)______ publicity, that the new products will enhance their happiness.

Hinglish

  • ​Late, positive degree है और  'Later', 'Late' शब्द की तुलनात्मक डिग्री है।
  • 'Latest', 'Late' की Superlative degree है।
  • Latter भी एक comparative degree है।
  • हम यह कहने के लिए superlative का उपयोग करते हैं कि कोई वस्तु या व्यक्ति समूह में सबसे अधिक है।
  • जब हम संज्ञा से पहले एक superlative adjective ('the tallest student') का उपयोग करते हैं, तो हम आम तौर पर इसका उपयोग 'the' के साथ करते हैं।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.

Key Points

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.

The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. 'Snatch a moment'.Key Points

  • The phrase "snatch a moment" is idiomatic and means to quickly seize or take advantage of a brief period of time.
  • It implies that the speaker is actively trying to find opportunities to be alone with the person being referred to (her) in order to express praise for her art.
  • The word "snatch" suggests a sense of urgency or haste in making use of the limited time available.

Therefore, the correct sentence is:-  I praised her art whenever I could snatch a moment alone with her and whisper in her ear, out of range of that husband of hers.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'Have called'.

Key Points

  •  The phrase "could more logically have called" is grammatically correct in the given sentence.
  • It is used to express a hypothetical or conditional possibility regarding the naming choice of a person.
  • In the context of the sentence, Rosie is being discussed in relation to her choice of name.
  • The verb phrase "could have called" indicates a past possibility or alternative action. It suggests that there was a logical option available to Rosie, but she did not choose it.
  • The word "could" indicates the ability or potential to do something, while "have called" is the past perfect tense of the verb "to call."

Therefore, the correct sentence is- 'Instead of calling of herself Rosie, she could more logically have called him Marco Polo'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'At first sight'.

Key Points

  • The phrase "at first sight" is grammatically correct in the given sentence.
  • It is used to describe an immediate impression or reaction upon seeing someone or something for the first time.
  • In the context of the sentence, the speaker is expressing their initial reaction to the man they encountered.
  • The phrase "at first sight" emphasizes that this naming decision was based solely on their initial visual perception of the man.
  • Grammatically, "at first sight" functions as an adverbial phrase modifying the verb "wanted to call."

Therefore, the correct sentence is:- I have, of course, no idea of the original Marco Polo's appearance, but I wanted to call this man Marco at first sight , and i have not bothered to associate him with any other name since.
